forces.title: AI/ML adoption reshaping clinical trial operations for CROs
forces.description: AI and machine learning adoption is increasing among Contract Research Organizations (CROs) and sponsors in clinical trials, albeit with most using it in under 25% of studies. This adoption signifies a structural shift towards technology-enabled clinical trial operations, impacting roles like trial monitoring and patient recruitment by offering opportunities to redesign work around AI. The focus is shifting from purely increasing staff numbers to leveraging technology for efficiency and overcoming persistent challenges like patient recruitment pressure.
forces.source_title: Clinical Trials Face Persistent Challenges—and New Opportunities

forces.title: Rising staffing costs and automation pressure Staffing & BPO demand
forces.description: Food and beverage producers in Ireland face persistent margin pressure from high staffing costs, leading to increased investment in automation, robotics, and integrated production methods. This trend aims to improve productivity and offset labor shortages, with some businesses bringing previously outsourced activities in-house. This acts as a headwind for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) and BPO (IN030303) providers, as clients seek to reduce reliance on external human resources and outsource services through internal automation, demanding more value-added solutions.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: AI's broad operational impact includes shifts in outsourcing strategies
forces.description: AI's economic value extends beyond labor cost reduction to enabling faster, better decision-making and driving broader operational changes. This includes reassessing insourcing and outsourcing strategies. As organizations implement AI, they must consider its implications for core processes and decision flows, which can lead to re-evaluation of current outsourced activities or demands for AI-enabled services from BPO providers. The focus shifts from mere automation to leveraging AI for improved business outcomes.
forces.source_title: The decision dividend: How AI creates economic value

forces.title: AI/automation enabling smaller, more skilled workforce in Hospitality
forces.description: The Irish hospitality sector is increasingly leveraging AI and automation for operational efficiency, focusing on areas like rostering, back-office processes, and energy monitoring. This technological adoption aims to reduce repetitive tasks and enable a shift towards a smaller, more skilled workforce, impacting demand for traditional staffing solutions. While this supports profit conversion for hospitality operators, it poses a structural change for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) and BPO (IN030303) providers, who will need to adapt their services to include more technology-enabled solutions and cater to a higher-skilled, often internal, workforce.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Gen AI transforming contract analysis and margin protection in BPO
forces.description: Gen AI is emerging as a powerful tool for contract intelligence, enabling organizations to optimize contract structures, identify profit leakage risks, and empower sales negotiations. This technology enhances the capabilities of Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) firms, particularly those offering legal process outsourcing (LPO) or F&A outsourcing services, by automating extraction of key commercial terms and transaction reconciliation. This represents an upside driver for BPO providers who can integrate AI into their offerings, allowing them to deliver more valuable and efficient services for clients seeking to protect margins and improve contract compliance.
forces.source_title: Pricing in distribution: A strategic growth engine

forces.title: Retail sector's recruitment challenges create tailwind for staffing firms
forces.description: The Irish retail convenience sector faces ongoing difficulties in recruiting and retaining personnel due to a "full employment" environment. This challenge intensifies retailers' focus on margin development and preservation, making external staffing and human capital services more attractive. The persistent demand for talent, coupled with the struggle to find and keep employees, represents a tailwind for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers, who can offer solutions for flexi staffing, permanent recruitment, and HR outsourcing to help retailers navigate these labor market pressures and ensure operational continuity.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Retail Convenience H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Outsourced domains attract AI transformation, boosting BPO innovation
forces.description: Enterprises undergoing AI transformation are finding that operational domains already outsourced or offshored offer attractive starting points for redesign due to faster implementation and lower organizational disruption. This creates an upside driver for BPO and Business Process Services (IN030303) providers who can offer AI-ready solutions, modular platforms, and expertise in intelligence architecture. The demand is for BPO providers that can integrate AI sustainably, leveraging structured data and vendor-agnostic orchestration to unlock enterprise-wide gains in speed, scalability, and efficiency.
forces.source_title: The symbiotic enterprise

forces.title: Norway's recruitment challenges ease overall, persist for skilled labor
forces.description: Norges Bank's Regional Network report indicates an easing of overall recruitment difficulties in Norway, with fewer contacts reporting full capacity utilization and a decline in labor supply constraints. Digital solutions are also reducing the need for some employees. However, challenges persist in recruiting specific skilled workers such as project managers, machine operators, carpenters, electricians, chefs, and drivers. This mixed environment presents both headwinds for general staffing services due to reduced demand, and potential tailwinds for specialized recruitment for skilled trades within Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302).
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 2/2026: Recruitment difficulties have eased somewhat

forces.title: Commercial services face headwinds from hesitancy, costs, and AI disruption
forces.description: Norwegian commercial services are experiencing mixed signals, with increased activity from defense, emergency preparedness, energy, and data center investments. However, significant headwinds arise from global turbulence, rising costs, and higher interest rates, leading to customer hesitation and postponed projects across various sectors, including strategic advisory services. Notably, some consultancy firms report reduced customer demand due to the emergence of artificial intelligence, posing a structural challenge for Management Consulting (IN030301) and other professional services within IG0303.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 2/2026: Recruitment difficulties have eased somewhat

forces.title: Integrated HR and payroll solutions drive efficiency in banking
forces.description: The banking sector is adopting streamlined HR and payroll solutions, as exemplified by a SACCO banking platform integrating Workpay's offerings. This indicates a structural shift towards enhanced efficiency in human capital management within financial institutions. For Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers, this trend highlights the growing demand for integrated, cloud-native HR and payroll services that can be seamlessly embedded into client operations, creating opportunities for specialized service offerings that reduce operational costs and strengthen banking portfolios through digital innovation.
forces.source_title: From potential to performance: A snapshot of African banking

forces.title: Complex maritime threats boost demand for security services
forces.description: The maritime industry faces an increasingly complex threat environment, encompassing physical risks like war, terrorism, and piracy, as well as digital threats such as cyberattacks and navigation system disruptions. This heightened risk landscape places stricter demands on risk assessments, preventive security measures, and incident handling capabilities for shipping companies. This serves as a significant tailwind for Security Services (IN030304) providers, creating increased demand for specialized maritime physical security guarding, aviation security operations (for cargo/port facilities), and alarm monitoring services to protect critical maritime infrastructure and operations.
forces.source_title: Maritime Outlook 2026

forces.title: Critical maritime skill shortages pose risk to Norwegian shipping
forces.description: The Norwegian shipping industry faces significant challenges in acquiring essential competencies, particularly operational experience at sea, along with electrical, automation, and digital skills over the next decade. This persistent skill gap is considered a key risk for the maritime cluster, potentially undermining its competitive strength. This creates opportunities for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers specializing in highly skilled maritime recruitment and training, as shipowners seek external support to address these critical talent shortages and maintain a robust base of Norwegian seafarers.
forces.source_title: Maritime Outlook 2026

forces.title: Supply chain resilience focus creates BPO opportunities for manufacturing
forces.description: Irish manufacturing firms are increasingly prioritizing supply chain visibility, resilience, and agility, driven by past geopolitical and economic shocks. As part of their strategic initiatives to manage risks and future-proof operations, they are implementing mitigating actions that include "outsourcing" alongside reshoring and dual supply. This focus creates a tailwind for BPO & Business Process Services (IN030303) providers, particularly those offering supply chain management BPO, as manufacturers seek external partners to help build and resource their operations teams, leveraging digital and AI to anchor supply chain decisions in data.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: AI deployment alters workforce and recruitment, prioritizing new skills
forces.description: Ireland's high rate of AI adoption is profoundly impacting the labor market, leading to a rebalancing of roles and evolving skill requirements. While not primarily causing job losses, AI deployment is prompting headcount reductions in some technology companies and a significant shift in recruitment strategies, with 60% of organizations now prioritizing AI-related capabilities. This represents a structural change for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers, necessitating a focus on reskilling, upskilling, and recruiting talent with specialized AI competencies, and a potential reduction in demand for traditional, routine task-based roles.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Healthcare providers face escalating staffing and regulatory costs
forces.description: Irish healthcare providers, particularly in residential care, are experiencing significant cost pressures from rising staffing expenses, including statutory minimum wage increases (6% in 2025, 4.8% in 2026) and increased remuneration thresholds for employment permits. The operational impact of the 50:50 staffing mix requirement and increasing care complexity further intensifies these cost burdens. This situation creates a challenging environment for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers working in healthcare, as clients seek cost-effective solutions amidst high labor expenses and complex regulatory compliance.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: AI adoption drives administrative efficiency in Irish healthcare
forces.description: Irish healthcare providers are increasingly adopting technology, including AI, to enhance administrative efficiency, compliance, rostering, and reporting. The Department of Health's 2026 AI for Care strategy aims to leverage AI for faster diagnostics, improved patient flow, and a potential 40% reduction in clinical documentation time. This trend presents a structural change for BPO & Business Process Services (IN030303) and Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers, as demand shifts towards AI-enabled solutions that can automate routine tasks and optimize workforce management in the healthcare sector, moving away from purely manual processes.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: AI streamlines BPO tasks like invoice processing and payroll
forces.description: AI's ability to optimize repetitive tasks such as invoice processing and payroll is highlighted as a transformative corporate application, moving beyond simple automation to expand decision-making capacity. This structural change significantly impacts BPO & Business Process Services (IN030303) and Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers, particularly those offering F&A outsourcing and payroll services. It drives demand for AI-enabled solutions that can accelerate processes, reduce errors, and deliver documentation rapidly, while also potentially reshaping the nature of human labor required for these tasks.
forces.source_title: The AI assembly line: Strategic imperatives for CEOs

forces.title: Manufacturing grapples with escalating costs and persistent skill gaps
forces.description: Irish manufacturing businesses are facing significant cost pressures from minimum wage increases, pension, and healthcare obligations, alongside high energy costs. This, coupled with persistent skills shortages, constrains growth potential and puts pressure on margins. These factors create a complex environment for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers, as manufacturers seek solutions to manage rising labor costs and fill critical skill gaps, potentially increasing demand for flexible staffing, training, and HR outsourcing services that offer cost efficiencies and access to specialized talent.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Manufacturing Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

forces.title: Manufacturing leverages AI to boost productivity and mitigate labor shortages
forces.description: Irish manufacturing is increasingly investing in AI, with 52% of businesses prioritizing it, to enhance productivity, improve efficiency, and address labor shortages through automation. This trend presents a structural change for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) and BPO & Business Process Services (IN030303) providers. While AI may reduce demand for some traditional labor-intensive tasks, it also creates new opportunities for providers offering AI-integrated services, specialized talent for automation implementation, and training for workforces adapting to AI-driven environments, necessitating a shift in service offerings.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Manufacturing Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

forces.title: Food sector's rising staff costs accelerate automation adoption
forces.description: The Irish food sector continues to grapple with increasing staff costs and recruitment challenges, leading to further adoption of automation to mitigate these pressures. This trend acts as a headwind for traditional Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers, as clients prioritize technological solutions over human labor for cost control and efficiency. Staffing firms will need to adapt their offerings, potentially focusing on recruitment for specialized roles in automation, or providing HR outsourcing services that integrate automation to remain competitive in a sector undergoing significant operational transformation.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Food and Drink Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

forces.title: Hospitality prioritizes AI to enhance efficiency and service quality
forces.description: The Irish hospitality sector is rapidly accelerating its adoption of technology, including AI, to achieve greater efficiencies and improve service quality. This structural shift impacts Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) and BPO & Business Process Services (IN030303) by reshaping the demand for human intervention in routine tasks. While it presents a challenge for traditional labor-intensive service models, it also creates opportunities for providers who can offer AI-driven solutions for managing operations, optimizing staff deployment, and enhancing customer experience, requiring a strategic pivot in service offerings.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Hospitality Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

forces.title: Escalating labor costs push demand for flexible staffing solutions
forces.description: Businesses in Ireland, particularly those reliant on food and beverage revenue, face intensifying labor cost pressures from rising national minimum wage (4.8% increase in 2026), new pension auto-enrolment, and increased employer PRSI contributions. This compels operators to conduct operational reviews, adopt tech-enabled labor optimization, and implement flexible service models. For Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers, this represents a tailwind for flexible staffing and HR outsourcing services that can help clients manage these escalating costs and optimize workforce deployment amidst persistent inflationary pressures.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Hospitality Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

forces.title: Construction labor shortages drive demand for staffing services in Ireland
forces.description: Ireland's construction sector is experiencing growing confidence with increasing workloads, leading to rising employment but also persistent labor shortages. Despite a slowdown in input cost inflation, the difficulty in finding sufficient workers remains a key challenge. This environment creates a tailwind for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers, as construction companies will increasingly rely on temporary, contract, and permanent recruitment services to meet their human resource needs and address the scarcity of skilled labor, supporting sectoral growth.
forces.source_title: 2025 Ireland economic outlook: Resilience amid global uncertainty

forces.title: Automation reduces graduate hiring and BPO demand for routine tasks
forces.description: The TMT sector in Ireland is experiencing a notable decline in graduate hiring due to companies automating routine tasks such as payroll and credit control. This signifies a structural shift towards AI-driven operations, impacting both Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) and BPO & Business Process Services (IN030303). While automation provides efficiency gains for clients, it acts as a headwind for providers of traditional payroll and F&A outsourcing, necessitating a re-evaluation of service models to focus on higher-value, AI-integrated solutions and specialized talent for evolving roles, rather than routine task processing.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

forces.title: AI-first talent intelligence platforms revolutionize staffing and recruitment
forces.description: The emergence and success of AI-first talent intelligence platforms, like Opening.io, are fundamentally redefining talent acquisition through machine learning to match candidates with opportunities. This represents a significant structural change for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers. The shift necessitates the adoption of advanced AI capabilities to enhance recruitment outcomes, moving from traditional matching methods to data-driven, predictive talent intelligence. This trend creates both competitive pressure and opportunities for staffing firms to innovate their offerings and remain at the forefront of talent solutions.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

forces.title: Digital currencies streamline global payroll and B2B payments
forces.description: Digital currencies, including stablecoins and tokenized deposits, are entering the mainstream, offering practical applications in cross-border remittances, B2B payments, and global payroll. This structural shift leverages programmable money for greater efficiency. For Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers offering payroll services, this presents an opportunity to innovate by adopting blockchain-based payment rails, enabling near-instant settlements and potentially reducing costs associated with international payroll, particularly in long-tail corridors and markets with unstable currencies.
forces.source_title: Global Payments Report 2025: The Future Is (Anything but) Stable

forces.title: Stablecoin-based global payroll poised for accelerated adoption
forces.description: Stablecoin-based payments, including global payroll and merchant payouts, are experiencing rapid adoption, particularly in regions where US dollar access, speed, and cost are critical drivers. With B2B stablecoin payments increasing 30-fold in two years to over $3 billion by 2025, this trend offers significant upside for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers. Those who integrate stablecoin payment rails can deliver faster, more cost-effective international payroll solutions, especially for cross-border workforces, leveraging emerging regulatory frameworks like Europe's MiCAR to build institutional confidence and drive scale.
forces.source_title: Global Payments Report 2025: The Future Is (Anything but) Stable

forces.title: Embedded payroll becomes critical for merchant operating platforms
forces.description: Integrated platforms like Shopify are increasingly offering comprehensive merchant-facing capabilities, including embedded payroll, invoicing, and fraud management, effectively creating a full operating system for businesses. This structural shift highlights the growing expectation for seamless, integrated financial services within business operations. For Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers specializing in payroll, this necessitates strategic partnerships or the development of integrated solutions that can be embedded into these platforms, moving beyond standalone offerings to provide a holistic, value-added service to merchants.
forces.source_title: Global Payments Report 2025: The Future Is (Anything but) Stable

forces.title: Hospitality profit pressures lead to anticipated staff cuts and reviews
forces.description: The Irish hotel and food services sectors are experiencing significant pressure on profit margins due to rising costs outpacing price increases, threatening the viability of smaller businesses. This has prompted many businesses to review operating models and staffing levels, with reports indicating anticipated staff cuts without government support. This presents a direct headwind for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers, as reduced demand for personnel and potential layoffs will impact recruitment and placement services across the hospitality industry, necessitating a focus on value retention strategies.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Hotel Sector H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

forces.title: Aviation sector struggles with staffing shortages impacting reliability
forces.description: The aviation sector faces persistent staffing shortages across its value chain, contributing to declining on-time performance and operational disruptions. While this is a challenge for airlines, it creates an ongoing demand for recruitment and flexible staffing solutions from Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers. However, the operational inefficiencies caused by these shortages also highlight the urgent need for airlines to adopt better analytics and data-driven operational decision-making, which could influence the nature of services required from staffing firms toward more specialized or tech-enabled solutions.
forces.source_title: The state of aviation

forces.title: Weakening net wage scheme risks Norwegian maritime job displacement
forces.description: The net wage scheme for seafarers is crucial for safeguarding Norwegian maritime expertise and recruitment. Over 70% of shipping companies indicate they would replace Norwegian seafarers with foreign ones if the scheme is weakened, while 40% would hire more Norwegians if the upper limit were removed. This highlights the scheme's critical role in maintaining competitive conditions and employment. Any weakening poses a significant key risk for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers and for Norwegian maritime employment, potentially leading to reduced demand for domestic recruitment and a shift to international staffing.
forces.source_title: Maritime Outlook 2025

forces.title: Mandatory Norwegian wages for foreign seafarers threaten domestic jobs
forces.description: The Norwegian government's proposal for mandatory Norwegian wage levels on foreign-flagged ships is a significant concern for the maritime industry. The Norwegian Shipowners' Association argues this violates EEA agreements and their impact assessment suggests it would paradoxically lead to a reduction of Norwegian seafarers. This presents a key risk for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers by potentially diminishing demand for Norwegian maritime personnel and shifting hiring practices to avoid increased costs, undermining efforts to safeguard domestic employment and competitiveness.
forces.source_title: Maritime Outlook 2025

forces.title: Healthcare workforce shortages drive demand for staffing solutions
forces.description: The Irish healthcare sector faces persistent workforce challenges, including skills shortages, intense competition for talent in a low unemployment environment, and high staff turnover (36.3% in nursing homes). An ageing population is driving a projected 3.5-4% annual growth in demand for healthcare assistants over the next 12 years. These factors create a strong tailwind for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers, offering significant opportunities for permanent recruitment, flexi staffing, and HR outsourcing services to address the critical talent gap in both public and private care settings.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Health Insights 2024 / Outlook 2025 February 2025

forces.title: Migrant HCA employment permits increase cost burden for healthcare providers
forces.description: Private healthcare providers in Ireland face a considerable cost burden due to increased minimum salary requirements for non-EEA Healthcare Assistant (HCA) employment permits, which rose by 10% from 2024 to €30,000. While migrant workers are essential, accounting for 30% of permits issued to the health sector, this regulatory change impacts the profitability of care providers. For Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) firms, this acts as a headwind by increasing the cost of placing migrant workers, potentially challenging their pricing strategies and requiring careful management of remuneration and compliance for international recruitment.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Health Insights 2024 / Outlook 2025 February 2025

forces.title: Irish hotels integrate AI for enhanced CXM and personalization
forces.description: Irish hotels are increasingly integrating AI, including AI-enabled CRM systems, to improve customer service and support personalization. This focus on building lasting customer relationships through data processing and insight-driven actions marks a structural shift in hospitality operations. For BPO & Business Process Services (IN030303) providers specializing in Customer Experience Management (CXM), this presents an opportunity to offer AI-integrated solutions that help hotels optimize guest data, deliver tailored experiences, and enhance brand loyalty, thereby creating demand for advanced BPO services in the sector.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Hotels 2024 Insights & 2024 Outlook January 2025

forces.title: Manufacturing faces ongoing challenges from labor costs and skill shortages
forces.description: The Irish manufacturing sector, despite overall optimism, continues to face significant challenges from elevated labor costs and persistent skill shortages, identified as top concerns by Eurochambres. This tight labor market, combined with rising minimum wage and social costs, strains competitive profiles. This creates a sustained tailwind for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers, who can offer crucial solutions for flexible staffing, specialized recruitment, and HR outsourcing to help manufacturers manage their workforce effectively and bridge critical skill gaps, ensuring operational continuity and competitiveness.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Manufacturing 2024 Insights and 2025 Outlook February 2025

viewpoints.title: Ireland's AI adoption reshapes workforce and recruitment, impacting staffing
viewpoints.description: Ireland exhibits high AI adoption (43% private sector, 36% public sector), surpassing the EU average. While AI's impact is largely role rebalancing rather than mass job losses, it significantly shifts recruitment strategies, with 60% of organizations prioritizing AI-related capabilities. This creates a cautious-negative outlook for traditional Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers, as demand for general recruitment may decrease due to automation, necessitating a strategic pivot towards AI-driven solutions and specialized talent acquisition and upskilling services.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

viewpoints.title: Norwegian maritime sector grapples with critical skill shortages and talent competition
viewpoints.description: The Norwegian Shipowners' Association highlights critical challenges in attracting and developing a skilled workforce for the maritime cluster, particularly in operational, ICT, and digital expertise. Intense competition for manpower, compounded by geopolitical shifts and military recruitment, poses a significant risk to the industry's competitive advantage. This presents a cautious-positive outlook for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers specializing in maritime recruitment and training, as the sector requires strategic staffing solutions and expertise development to bridge persistent skill gaps.

viewpoints.title: AI transforms healthcare by automating administrative tasks and freeing clinicians
viewpoints.description: A KPMG report, cited by Bank of Ireland, indicates that AI is significantly reshaping healthcare operations, with 65% of global leaders reporting its impact. In Ireland, AI is crucial for addressing workforce shortages and rising demand by supporting earlier diagnoses, optimizing resource use, and notably reducing administrative tasks. This creates a cautious-positive outlook for BPO (IN030303) and HR outsourcing (IN030302) services that can integrate AI for administrative efficiency, allowing for cost savings and the redeployment of human capital to direct patient care roles.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Healthcare H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

viewpoints.title: Hospitality reports eased recruitment challenges, prioritizing staff well-being
viewpoints.description: Fáilte Ireland's Tourism Career Update, highlighted by Bank of Ireland, notes that recruitment and retention in the Irish hospitality sector have become "less difficult for the third year in a row." This improvement is linked to an increased focus on staff well-being, including flexible rostering, training, and automation of repetitive tasks. This presents a cautious-negative outlook for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers that primarily rely on acute labor shortages, as improved internal retention could lead to decreased demand for external hiring services, necessitating a pivot towards value-added HR consulting and technology-enabled solutions.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Hotels 2024 Insights & 2024 Outlook January 2025

viewpoints.title: AI emergence reduces customer demand for consultancy services in Norway
viewpoints.description: Norges Bank's Regional Network report reveals that some Norwegian consultancy firms are experiencing a reduction in customer demand due to the increasing adoption of artificial intelligence. This trend signals a cautious-negative outlook for Management Consulting (IN030301), as clients leverage AI for tasks traditionally handled by consultants, leading to a shift in service requirements. Consulting firms must adapt by integrating AI into their methodologies and focusing on delivering higher-value strategic guidance that complements, rather than competes with, AI capabilities to remain relevant.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 2/2026: Recruitment difficulties have eased somewhat

viewpoints.title: Persistent labor shortages in Ireland bolster Staffing & Human Capital sector
viewpoints.description: Across multiple Irish sectors, including retail, healthcare, and manufacturing, businesses consistently face significant challenges in recruitment and retention due to a "full employment" environment and persistent skills shortages. This sustained demand for personnel, coupled with rising labor costs, creates a positive outlook for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers. These firms are well-positioned to offer essential services like flexible staffing, permanent recruitment, and HR outsourcing, helping client sectors navigate talent scarcity and effectively manage their workforces amidst competitive labor market conditions.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Retail Convenience H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: Irish staffing firms benefit from rising labor costs driving flexible solutions
viewpoints.description: Businesses in Ireland, especially in hospitality, are grappling with intensifying labor cost pressures from rising national minimum wages, new pension auto-enrolment, and increased employer PRSI contributions. This compels operators to prioritize operational reviews, tech-enabled labor optimization, and flexible service models. This environment creates a positive outlook for Staffing & Human Capital (IN030302) providers, as demand for flexible staffing, temporary workers, and HR outsourcing services grows. Firms offering adaptable solutions for cost management and workforce optimization are well-positioned for growth.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Hospitality Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

viewpoints.title: Institutional catering expects strong growth in Ireland's foodservice sector
viewpoints.description: Bord Bia forecasts a 5% growth in Irish foodservices for the coming year, with institutional catering and the "Limited Services sector" anticipated to experience a stronger increase. This positive outlook for institutional catering (IN030305) is driven by its increasing market share over recent years, indicating a growing reliance on outsourced catering solutions by various institutions. This trend positions Facilities & Support Services firms offering institutional catering for robust demand and expansion within Ireland's evolving foodservice landscape, highlighting opportunities for long-tenure contracts in this segment.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Hospitality Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

demand_drivers.driver: Efficiency and speed in cross-border payments
demand_drivers.description: Stablecoin payroll offers near-instant settlement and potentially lower costs for international transactions, appealing to businesses with global workforces seeking faster and more transparent payment rails.

demand_drivers.driver: Reduced reliance on traditional banking infrastructure
demand_drivers.description: Digital currencies can bypass legacy banking systems, offering greater accessibility and speed, especially in regions with unstable currencies or less developed financial infrastructure, thereby increasing adoption in global payroll.

new_opportunities.description: Significant growth potential given current low adoption rates (<1%) and the benefits of real-time payments, especially in emerging markets and for B2B cross-border transactions, as institutional confidence grows with regulatory clarity.

market_sizing.methodology: Less than 1% of Payroll fintech Remote's customers have adopted global stablecoin payroll as of 2025. Stablecoins reached a market capitalization of $270 billion by August 2025, but real-world payments account for only about 1% of transaction volume, indicating very early-stage adoption.
market_sizing.source_title: Global Payments Report 2025: The Future Is (Anything but) Stable

demand_drivers.driver: Ageing population and increasing healthcare needs
demand_drivers.description: The rising proportion of individuals aged 65 and older in Ireland directly increases the demand for healthcare services, especially for direct care roles like HCAs, ensuring sustained growth.

demand_drivers.driver: High staff turnover in private care settings
demand_drivers.description: Private nursing homes and home care settings experience significantly higher staff turnover (e.g., 36.3% in nursing homes), necessitating continuous recruitment efforts and driving demand for new HCA hires.

pnl_drivers.driver: Increased cost burden from employment permits
pnl_drivers.description: The €30,000 minimum salary requirement for non-EEA HCA employment permits, increasing by 10% from 2024, imposes a considerable cost burden on private sector providers, impacting their P&L.

market_sizing.methodology: Demand for healthcare assistants (HCAs) is projected to require an annual growth rate of 3.5% to 4% over the next 12 years in Ireland, driven by an ageing population and increasing healthcare needs. This growth is particularly urgent in private nursing home and home care settings where staff turnover rates exceed those of HSE facilities.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Health Insights 2024 / Outlook 2025 February 2025
